```{r}
rm(list=ls())
library(knitr)
library(spaMM)
library(tidyverse)
library(splines)
library(foreach)
library(doParallel)
library(rcdd)


IPM_data <- read.csv("../data/donneesIPM.csv") #data usual format for IPM
#remove individuals Age and Size unknown
centauree_data <- IPM_data[!is.na(IPM_data$Size0Mars) & !is.na(IPM_data$Age),]
centauree_data$Age[centauree_data$Age > 8] <- 8

spaMM.options(separation_max=70)
```


Establishment rate 
Relationship between number of seedlings observed per quadrat on year t depending on the number of capitula observed on the same quadrat on year t-1

First we used the predicted values to replace missing data using model Cptlglm1 and next we create a dataset with nb of seed heads (capitula) and nb of seedlings the previous year

```{r}
cptldata <- centauree_data[centauree_data$Flowering!=0,]
Cptlglm1 <- fitme(log(Capitule) ~ 1  + Size0Mars + (Age|year), 
                  data=cptldata)

cptldata_predi <- IPM_data[IPM_data$Flowering==1,] %>%
  mutate(Capitule = ifelse(is.na(Capitule),exp(predict(Cptlglm1)),Capitule))

#Number of seedlings
plt <- IPM_data %>%
filter(Age ==1) %>% 
  summarise(Plantules = n(), .by= c(Quadrat,year))

#Number of capitula with a one-year delay
cptl <- cptldata_predi %>% 
  group_by(Quadrat,year,Pop) %>% 
  summarize(Capitule = sum(Capitule),.groups="drop")
cptl$year <- cptl$year+1


#Make the dataset Number of seedlings and capitulas per quadrat for each year
qq <- unique(IPM_data$Quadrat)
Pop <- NULL
for (i in 1:length(qq)) {
  Pop[i] <- unique(IPM_data$Pop[IPM_data$Quadrat==qq[i]])}
rer <- cbind(qq,Pop)
annee <- unique(IPM_data$year)
rer2 <- do.call(rbind, replicate(length(annee), rer, simplify = FALSE))
annee <- rep(annee,length(qq))
annee <- sort(annee)

donnees <- data.frame(rer2,annee)
names(donnees) <- c("Quadrat", "Pop","year")
class(donnees$Quadrat) <- "numeric"
class(donnees$Pop) <- "string"
donnees$Seedling <- 0
donnees$Capitula <- 0

#add the number of seedlings
donnees <- donnees %>%
  left_join(
    plt %>% select(Quadrat, year,Plantules),
    by = c("Quadrat", "year")
  ) %>%
  mutate(Seedling = ifelse(is.na(Plantules), Seedling, Plantules)) %>%
  select(-Plantules)

#Add the number of seed heads 
donnees <- donnees %>%
  left_join(
    cptl %>% select(Quadrat, year, Capitule),
    by = c("Quadrat", "year")
  ) %>%
  mutate(Capitula = ifelse(is.na(Capitule), Capitula, Capitule)) %>%
  select(-Capitule)


#remove the first year (no data)
donnees <- subset(donnees, donnees$year>1994)
```



The number of seedlings observed in a quadrat in year t depend on :

1- number of migrants, noted mu
2- number of capitula observed in the same quadrat in year t-1 * the establishment rate, Estb

$$seedlings_t = \mu + Estb * capitula_{t-1}$$

Because of the Poisson distribution of the Nb of seedlings, the model is :


$$seedlings_t = log(\mu + Estb * capitula_{t-1})$$
We also assume log(*Gamma random effect*)

We first define an objective function that gives the (negative) log likelihood of the model fitted with an offset of the form $\log(\mu+Estb*capitula) for *given* values of the fixed effects coefficients $\mu$ and $\Estb$ (therefore, only the random effects are fitted):


```{r Clapefn}
Clapefn <- function(v, data, 
                    formula, # the formula will contain offset(logfixef)
                    rand.family, 
                    return.fit=FALSE) {
  fixef <- v[1] + v[2] * data$Capitula
  data$logfixef <- log(fixef)
  fit <- fitme(formula=formula, data=data,
              rand.family=rand.family, family=poisson(log) )
  if (return.fit) {fit} else {-logLik(fit)}
}
```

Next we use an optimization function to estimate the coefficients v[1] and v[2] (i.e. mu and Estb)
Note that using `rand.family=Gamma(log)` below implies that the mean value of the random effect is 1. Otherwise, this might complicate the interpretation of the fits below. Alternatively, we could have assumed `exp(rnorm(.))` in the data simulation, and the default Gaussian distribution for the random effects in the statistical model. 

```{r optr, cache=TRUE}
lower <- c(1e-6,1e-6)
upper <- c(200,200)
(optr <- (spaMM::.safe_opt(
  init=c(1,0.1),objfn = Clapefn,
  data=donnees, lower = lower, upper=upper,
  verbose = FALSE,LowUp = list(lower=lower, upper=upper),
  formula=Seedling ~ offset(logfixef) + 0 + (1|Pop:year), # Note the +0+ ...
  rand.family=Gamma(log),
  return.fit=FALSE
)))
optr$solution
```


The fitted coefficients are `r optr$solution`, first term is mu and second term is Estb

Here I (François Rousset) used an undocumented function of `spaMM`, `spaMM::.safe_opt` because I (FR) know well its syntax, and it deals with various potential problems. But other optimizers could be used.

Get the final fit:
```{r Clapefit}
(Clapefit <- Clapefn(optr$solution, data=donnees, 
         formula=Seedling ~ offset(logfixef) + 0 + (1|Pop:year),
         rand.family=Gamma(log), return.fit=TRUE) )
```

<!-- The `lambda` value is reasonably close to its target value which is here the scale parameter of the Gamma distribution, `scale=0.5` above. -->

I have used `rand.family=Gamma(log)` to match the data simulation, but one could assume default gaussian random effects, with often give similar fits.


We now have the number of seedlings predicted as a function of the number of seed heads observed

```{r plot}
plot(Clapefit, which="predict", xlim=c(0,170), ylim=c(0,170))
```

Comparaison observed/predicted per year

```{r}

donnees$pred_seedling <- predict(Clapefit)[,1]

bilan <- donnees %>% 
    group_by(year) %>%
    summarize(Seedling=sum(Seedling), pred_seedling=sum(pred_seedling), Capitula=sum(Capitula))

bilan$Estb <- bilan$Seedling/bilan$Capitula
bilan$pred <- bilan$pred_seedling/bilan$Capitula

bilan %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = Estb)) +
  geom_line(col="red") +
  geom_line(aes(y= pred), col="green") +
  labs(y="Establishment rate",
       x="Year",
       subtitle = "Red line : mean of observed values
       Green line : predicted value") +
    theme_minimal()
```



Integration in IPM

Establishment rate is used to convert number of capitula produced in year t to nb of seedlings in year t+1.  More precisely :

Density of individuals of size y and age 1 (seedling) at t from reproduction of a plant of size x and age a at t :
$$F_a(x,y,t)=f_a(x)c_a(x)\omega(y)Estb$$

In the R script 

#Combine fecundity and flowering probability 
fyx0 <- function(x , a, Estbl, Beta = 0) {
  p.flow <- flr1(x, a, Beta) #flowering probability
  n.captl <- numbofcap(x, a) #number of capitula per flowering plant
  Estbl <- Estbli(populations,annees)
  
  feco <- p.flow * n.captl * Estbl
  return(feco)
}
